title: Start here: how to use this guide
one: What you are making, how a chapter works, and the three rules.

screens.title: See what your program is, before you make it
screens.goal: My program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file that saves each pupil.

open.what: Your program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file. This part shows the whole thing, then where it lives in Visual Studio.
open.does: When you have read it, you know the five forms and how to run them.

screens.title: Meet the four words you will see a lot
screens.done: you have read the four words
screens.goal: I know what a form, a control, a property and IntelliSense are.

blocks.p: This guide helps you create your Unit 5 program, one part at a time.

words: One of the pages of your program. The login is a form. The quiz is a form.
Anything you put on a form: a button, a text box, a panel, a label.
A setting of a control, like its Name or its Text. The Properties window lists them.
The list that pops up as you type code. It knows every name in your program.
blocks.intro: Click any marked word to see what it means.

screens.title: See the five forms and the one file
screens.done: you have looked at the picture and read the line under it
screens.goal: My program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file that saves each pupil.

blocks.p: Here is the whole program, five forms and one file.

drawn.alt: Five cards: Login, Data entry, Quiz, Reaction test and Report, joined by arrows, with a note card for the file pupilStats.txt.
drawn.say: Each card is one [[form|0]], and the arrows are the buttons between them.
cards: Five panels, where everything is typed in.
Twelve pictures and a ten-second clock.
A table of every saved pupil.
Your program saves each pupil's results in here, one line per pupil.

blocks.p: You have made some of these already, and the home page shows which parts are done.

blocks.watch: Every form has a name that starts with frm. You will see those names in the code.

screens.title: See where your forms live
screens.done: you have found Solution Explorer on the right
screens.goal: Solution Explorer lists my forms and Global.cs, on the right of Visual Studio.

blocks.p: Everything in your project is listed in Solution Explorer, on the right of Visual Studio.

frames.title: Solution Explorer

frames.alt: Solution Explorer on the right of Visual Studio 2019, listing the five forms and Global.cs
frames.say: Solution Explorer is on the right, with every form and Global.cs listed.

frames.watch: Watch for Global.cs listed under the five forms

blocks.watch: Global.cs is listed under the five forms. It is the file that remembers things between forms.

screens.title: Open a form's Design tab and its code tab
screens.done: you have opened one form's code
screens.goal: Double-clicking a form opens the Design tab, and View Code opens the code tab.

blocks.p: Each form has a Design tab for the form and a code tab for its code.

frames.title: Design tab and code tab

frames.alt: The right-click menu of a form with View Code highlighted
frames.say: Double-click a form for its Design tab. Right-click it for View Code.

frames.watch: Watch for View Code in the right-click menu

blocks.p: Closing a tab deletes nothing. Double-click the form to open it again.

screens.title: Start your program with the green arrow
screens.done: you have seen the green Start arrow
screens.goal: The green Start arrow runs my program.

blocks.p: You will run your program a lot, so here is how to start it.

frames.title: Running your program

frames.alt: The toolbar with the green Start arrow
frames.say: The green Start arrow at the top runs your program.

frames.watch: Watch for the green Start arrow at the top

blocks.watch: Use the green arrow and the menus, never keyboard shortcuts. In a browser tab, a shortcut can reload the page.

screens.title: Stop your program with the red square
screens.done: you have seen the red Stop square
screens.goal: The red square stops my program.

blocks.p: While your program runs, the green arrow becomes a red Stop square.

frames.title: Stopping your program

frames.alt: The toolbar while the program runs, with the red Stop square
frames.say: Press the red Stop square to stop your program.

frames.watch: Watch the green arrow turn into a red square

blocks.watch: Stop your program before you go back to typing code.

screens.title: See how a chapter works and where you are up to
screens.goal: Every chapter has the same shape, and the home page shows me my next job.

open.what: Every chapter has the same shape. The home page shows which parts are done and which part is next.
open.does: When you have read it, you can find your next job on any day.

screens.title: See what a chapter looks like
screens.done: you have looked at the picture and read the lines under it
screens.goal: A chapter is a row of parts, each part is a few screens, and each screen has one job.

blocks.p: This guide is split into chapters.
One chapter is one part of your program, like the login or the quiz.

drawn.alt: A small drawn chapter: a row of part pills, a list of three steps with tick boxes, and a big button at the foot.
drawn.say: A chapter is a row of parts, each a few screens.

blocks.p: Every chapter starts by checking what you need, and ends with a Try it screen.

screens.title: Mark a screen done with the big button
screens.done: you know what the big button at the bottom does
screens.goal: The big button at the bottom ticks a screen off and moves me on.

blocks.p: Each screen says what you are making, and when it is done.
When you have done a screen, press the big button at the bottom.
It ticks the screen and moves you on to the next one.

blocks.watch: Your ticks are saved to your school account. Next lesson, the guide opens where you left off.

screens.title: Open the first part that is not ticked
screens.done: you know how to find your next job on the home page
screens.goal: The home page lists every part in order, I tick what I have done, and I open the first part that is not ticked.

blocks.p: The home page is called Where am I up to? and it lists every part in order.
Tick the parts you have already done, then open the first part that is not ticked.
If you were away, this is how you pick up where you were.

drawn.alt: One chapter card from the home page: the number, the title, a progress ring that fills as you tick, an Open button and a smaller I did this already button.
drawn.say: The grey button is for a part you made before this guide.

blocks.watch: Only press I did this already if it is true, because the guide cannot check. Your program will.

screens.title: Meet the three rules you keep all the way through
screens.goal: Three rules run through every chapter of this guide.

open.what: Three rules run through every chapter. My names are not your names. IntelliSense types names for you. You type every line yourself.
open.does: When you keep them, red lines are rare and your names stay your own.

screens.title: Meet rule 1: my names are not your names
screens.done: you know that MY names may differ from YOUR names
screens.goal: The guide shows the names Mr Gartland gave his controls, and I use the names I gave mine.

blocks.p: Every [[control|1]] in your program has a name, like tbxSurname, and the code uses those names.
This guide shows MY example with MY names, and YOUR names may be different.

blocks.watch: When you see one of my names, read it as the name YOU gave that control.

screens.title: Click a control to find its name
screens.done: you know that one click in the Design tab picks a control
screens.goal: To find a control's name, I click it once in the Design tab.

blocks.p: The name is a [[property|2]] of the control, one of its settings.

frames.title: Finding a control's name

frames.alt: The Design tab with one text box clicked once
frames.say: In the Design tab, click the control once.

frames.watch: Watch the control get small handles when it is clicked

screens.title: Read the name at the top of the Properties window
screens.done: you know where to find the name of any control
screens.goal: The name sits beside Name at the top of the Properties window.

blocks.p: The Properties window lists the settings of the control you clicked.

frames.title: The Name line

frames.alt: The Properties window with the name tbxSurname at the top
frames.say: At the top of the Properties window, the name sits beside Name.

frames.watch: Watch the Name line at the top of the Properties window

blocks.watch: If the Properties window is not there, open the View menu and click Properties Window.

screens.title: Meet rule 2: let IntelliSense type the name
screens.done: you have watched the list pop up and finish a name
screens.goal: When I type the first letters of a name, IntelliSense lists the names in my program and Tab finishes it.

blocks.p: [[IntelliSense|3]] is the list that pops up as you type code.
It knows every name in your program and types most of each one for you.

screens.title: See the first letters typed on a new line
screens.done: you have seen the first letters typed on a new line
screens.goal: I type the first letters of a name on a new line.

blocks.p: Here is the real list in Visual Studio 2019, in three pictures.

frames.title: The real list: picture 1 of 3

frames.alt: The code tab with pnl typed on a new line
frames.say: Type the first letters of the name.

frames.watch: Watch the letters pnl typed on a new line

screens.title: See the list pop up with every matching name
screens.done: you have seen the list pop up under the letters
screens.goal: The list pops up with every matching name in my program.

blocks.p: As soon as you type, the list pops up under the letters.

frames.title: The real list: picture 2 of 3

frames.alt: The IntelliSense list open under pnl, showing the matching names
frames.say: The list pops up with every matching name in YOUR program.

frames.watch: Watch the list pop up as pnl is typed

blocks.watch: If a name is not in the list, your control has a different name. Check it in the Properties window.

screens.title: See Tab type the whole name
screens.done: you know that Tab types the name from the list
screens.goal: Tab types the name for me, spelt right.

blocks.p: Press Tab and the name is typed for you, spelt right.

frames.title: The real list: picture 3 of 3

frames.alt: The line completed to a panel name
frames.say: Press Tab. The name is typed for you, spelt right.

frames.watch: Watch the name get typed when Tab is pressed

screens.title: Meet rule 3: you type every line yourself
screens.done: you have read the three practice lines
screens.goal: I cannot copy code from the guide, I type it, and I read each line as I type it.

blocks.p: You cannot copy code from this guide, so you type every line yourself.
Typing is how it sticks in your head.
You do not type these anywhere yet. Read them and see how they look.

code.title: Three lines to try, for practice only
code.where: nowhere yet. This one is only for trying the rule.
partLines: Three lines you will meet again
Switch off one panel, switch on the next, hide a button. Each line ends with a semicolon.

blocks.watch: Read each line as you type it, so you know what it does.

screens.title: Try to copy a line from the guide
screens.done: you have tried to copy a line and the guide said no
screens.goal: I have tried to copy a line and seen the guide refuse.

blocks.p: Go back one screen and try to copy a line from the code box there.

steps.do: Select a line in the box, then right-click it or drag it.
steps.see: The guide says no, with a small message. You type it instead.

screens.title: See what a red line means
screens.done: you know what a red wiggly line means and where the Error List is
screens.goal: A red wiggly line means Visual Studio does not understand that line, and the Error List takes me to it.

blocks.p: Sometimes a line gets a red wiggly underline.
That means Visual Studio does not understand it yet.

frames.title: Finding an error

frames.alt: A code line with a red wiggly underline under a misspelt name
frames.say: A red wiggly line under a word.

frames.alt: The Error List at the bottom of Visual Studio 2019 with one error
frames.say: The Error List at the bottom names the problem.

frames.alt: The cursor on the line after double-clicking the error
frames.say: Double-click the error. The cursor jumps to the line.

frames.watch: Watch the Error List name the line with the red wiggle

blocks.watch: Most red lines are a name spelt differently from the control. Check the name in the Properties window.

screens.title: Check your program builds before you run it
screens.done: you have seen Build succeeded at the bottom left
screens.goal: Build Solution checks every line, and Build succeeded at the bottom left means I can run it.

blocks.p: Build before you run, because building checks every line of your code.

frames.title: Building

frames.alt: The Build menu open with Build Solution highlighted
frames.say: Open the Build menu and choose Build Solution.

frames.alt: The bottom left of Visual Studio 2019 saying Build succeeded

frames.watch: Watch for Build succeeded at the bottom left

blocks.watch: If the bottom left says Build failed, go back one screen and find the red line.
